summary: The scheduler is sound as a driver that never runs a unit twice and never spends by accident: pg_cron (*/5 and 02:18 UTC) signs a {tick, kind} body with HMAC-SHA256 from two Vault secrets, the Node route (maxDuration 60) runs seven categories in a fixed order under 90 s leases, a 48 s start cutoff, per-category minimum starts (generation 43 s) and a 53 s abort, and records every tick in marketing_ticks. Its limits are latency and headroom, not correctness. One generation job per 5-minute tick and at most five collection operations per tick make a 4-brief night take about 36-50 minutes of wall time for 3-4 minutes of work (fourth post in review around 22:36 from a 22:00 Prague start under ideal conditions, 22:45-22:50 with Apify profiles or a second media pass; computed from code constants, not measured live). A job renders only after its 45 s model budget and under the tick's 53 s abort, so a slow two-attempt job can lose its model spend with no replay. A five-kit pre-render (40 slides, about 6-10 s of rendering plus about 16 s of sequential four-round-trip uploads) cannot live inside the generation step, but fits as an overnight render category (one post per tick, 4 ticks for 4 posts) or as on-demand single-kit renders of 2-4 s in a user route; a queue or worker is not needed for 4 posts a day. Production still lacks marketing_scheduler_prune_ticks and the history-prune job, so every daily tick since 22 Oct records retention: scheduler-state-unavailable while docs/marketing-scheduling.md presents both as live. The owner must understand 4 pg_cron jobs, 3 Vercel crons, 8 SQL functions, 8 leases, 7+3 categories, 7 statuses, 6 behaviour switches plus 9 pilot/manual variables that do nothing in production, and 23 marketing routes including dormant n8n-era entry points. The scheduler's unit tests (67) pass in 1.65 s; the end-to-end dry-day harness is green in CI on Node 22 but fails on this machine's Node 26 at project resolution.

facts.fact: Signing: scheduler_post reads marketing_scheduler_url and marketing_scheduler_secret from Vault, refuses a URL whose path is not exactly /api/marketing/tick or a secret under 32 chars or with whitespace, builds {tick: gen_random_uuid(), kind}, and sends Authorization: Bearer, X-Marketing-Timestamp and X-Marketing-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp||'.'||body)) with a 55 s pg_net timeout.

facts.fact: Budgets: no category starts after 48 s (soft), every abort signal fires at 53 s (hard), and each category needs a minimum of the soft budget left: collection 20 s, media 25 s, briefs 5 s, generation 43 s, publishing 15 s (30 s when live), reconciliation 5 s, token 16 s, renewal 15 s, purge 10 s, retention 1 s.
